title: The irrelevant babble effect in individuals with autism spectrum disorder
author: Lejla Alikadic

steps.title: Recruit and Screen Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit participants based on specific eligibility criteria and obtain written informed consent.

substeps.instruction: Ensure participants meet eligibility criteria: formal diagnosis of autistic disorder (previously 'high-functioning'), Asperger's disorder, autism spectrum disorder 'without accompanying intellectual impairment/without accompanying language impairment' (DSM-IV-TR, DSM-5), or equivalent diagnoses (ICD-10, ICD-11).
Obtain written informed consent from all participants.

steps.title: Conduct Pretests
steps.instruction: Perform pretests to measure intellectual and language abilities and autism severity.

steps.title: Prepare Experimental Environment
steps.instruction: Seat participants individually in a sound-attenuated booth in the university laboratory.

steps.title: Perform Training Block
steps.instruction: Administer a training block consisting of four trials of the visual-verbal serial recall task without auditory distractors.

steps.title: Perform Experimental Block
steps.instruction: Administer the experimental block consisting of 72 trials (12 trials per condition) using a 2 x 2 x 3 mixed design.

substeps.instruction: Present sequences of eight digits from the set {1, 2, ..., 9} on a computer screen at a rate of 1 Hz (800 ms on, 200 ms off).

Simultaneously present auditory distractors via headphones in randomized order across six conditions: single-channel speech soft, single-channel speech loud, dual-channel speech soft, dual-channel speech loud, multi-channel speech soft, and multi-channel speech loud.
Score serial recall performance using a strict serial-recall criterion.

steps.title: Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Perform statistical analysis on the collected serial recall data.

substeps.instruction: Run a 2 x 2 x 3 repeated-measures MANOVA with group (autistic vs. nonautistic) as between-subjects factor, and intensity (low, high) and complexity (single, dual, multi-channel speech) as within-subjects factors.

Use orthogonal contrasts on the auditory condition variable to test for the irrelevant babble effect (decrease in disruption in multi-channel conditions relative to single- and dual-channel combined).
Test for an intensity effect (increase in disruption in high-intensity conditions relative to low-intensity conditions).
Conduct exploratory analyses to examine if the irrelevant babble and intensity effects were subject to habituation.
